located within the Los Angeles, California fashion district (referred to hereafter as the
“Los Angeles Fashion District GTO”).12 The Los Angeles Fashion District GTO applied
to certain specified types of “Covered Businesses,” including “perfume stores,” in a
“Covered Geographic Area” that encompassed A&S’s Fine Fragrance location at 501
East Olympic Boulevard.13

course of its trade or business, received currency in excess of $3,000 in one transaction
or two or more related transactions in a 24-hour period, to report such transactions
electronically to FinCEN.14 The Los Angeles Fashion District GTO was effective from
October 9, 2014 through April 6, 2015.

statutory.answer: Yes, the conduct described falls within 5324(a)(3) prohibits structuring.
statutory.label: entailment
statutory.reasoning: Under 31 U.S.C. § 5324(a)(3), it is unlawful to structure transactions to evade reporting requirements. The fact pattern shows seven transactions totaling $8,043.01, including five cash withdrawals of $505.25, $675.24, $215.77, $682.20, $730.55, and $438.90, all occurring near transit hubs. These small, fragmented cash withdrawals are indicative of an attempt to avoid the $10,000 reporting threshold. The proximity of these transactions to the threshold and the pattern of multiple small cash movements satisfy the elements of structuring under 5324(a)(3).
